title: Equalizer right adjoint for an augmented simplicial topos
statement: Let $(\mathcal E_n,f_\alpha^{-1})$ be a coherent simplicial diagram of sites/topoi indexed by $\Delta^{op}$ [def-weil-pbc-topos] [def-weil-size-convention], with total site $\mathcal E_{\mathrm{tot}}$ constructed by [lem-trf-slice-site-total-pseudofunctor]. Let $\mathcal D$ be a topos [def-weil-pbc-topos] with inverse-image functors $a_n^{-1}:\mathcal D\to\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal E_n)$ and coherent identifications $f_\alpha^{-1}a_p^{-1}\cong a_q^{-1}$ for every $\alpha:[p]\to[q]$, where $f_\alpha:\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal E_q)\to\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal E_p)$ is the corresponding component geometric morphism. Use the equivalence of $\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{tot}})$ with compatible systems $(F_n,t_\alpha)$ (with arbitrary transition maps) supplied by [lem-trf-slice-site-total-systems]. Then $G\mapsto(a_n^{-1}G)_n$, with its canonical transitions, defines a geometric morphism [def-trf-geometric-morphism] from $\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{tot}})$ to $\mathcal D$. Its right adjoint sends a compatible system $(F_n,t_\alpha)$ to the equalizer in $\mathcal D$ of the two maps $a_{0,*}F_0\rightrightarrows a_{1,*}F_1$ associated to the two maps $[0]\to[1]$. The equalizer is characterized by the fact that a map into it is exactly a compatible family of maps $a_n^{-1}G\to F_n$; the identity and cocycle laws follow from the coherence data.

proof.text: By the total-site systems equivalence, a sheaf on the total site is a compatible family of component sheaves with transition maps satisfying the identity and composition cocycles. For $G\in\mathcal D$, put the component in degree $n$ equal to $a_n^{-1}G$ and use the given coherent identifications $f_\alpha^{-1}a_q^{-1}G\cong a_p^{-1}G$ as its transitions. The coherence laws make this a compatible system, hence an object of $\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{tot}})$.

source.place: Tag 0D70, lemma-augmentation-site, construction of the component inverse images and the total inverse image

proof.text: Each $a_n^{-1}$ is an inverse-image functor, so it preserves finite limits. Limits of compatible systems are computed componentwise, with transitions induced by the universal properties; therefore $G\mapsto(a_n^{-1}G)_n$ preserves finite limits. This is the inverse-image part of the required geometric-morphism datum.

source.place: Tag 0D70, lemma-augmentation-site, verification that the inverse image is exact

proof.text: For a compatible system $F=(F_n,t_\alpha)$, form the two maps $d_0,d_1:a_{0,*}F_0\rightrightarrows a_{1,*}F_1$ by applying the two maps $[0]\to[1]$, inserting the unit into the corresponding inverse-image/direct-image adjunction, and then using the transition of $F$. Let $a_*F$ be their equalizer in $\mathcal D$. Equalizers exist because $\mathcal D$ is a topos, and the construction is functorial in maps of compatible systems.

source.place: Tag 0D70, lemma-augmentation-site, equalizer definition of the direct image

proof.text: The equalizer universal property identifies a map $G\to a_*F$ with a map $G\to a_{0,*}F_0$ whose two composites with $d_0,d_1$ agree. By the adjunction $a_0^{-1}\dashv a_{0,*}$ this is a degree-zero map $a_0^{-1}G\to F_0$ satisfying the vertex/edge compatibility. For each $n$ and each vertex $[0]\to[n]$, use the corresponding transition and the coherent identifications to propagate this map to a component map $a_n^{-1}G\to F_n$. Any two vertices of $[n]$ are the endpoints of an order map $[1]\to[n]$, so the equalizer condition makes the propagated maps equal. The same coherence then makes them commute with every simplicial operator and satisfy the identity and composition laws. Conversely, a compatible family of component maps restricts in degree zero to a map satisfying the equalizer condition, and the two constructions are inverse and natural in $G$ and $F$.

source.place: Tag 0D70, lemma-augmentation-site, the cosimplicial-map argument and the vertex/edge argument

proof.text: The natural bijections of the preceding step give $G\mapsto(a_n^{-1}G)_n$ as a left adjoint to $a_*$. Together with finite-limit preservation from Step 2, this is a geometric morphism in the sense of [def-trf-geometric-morphism], and Step 3 gives the asserted equalizer formula for its right adjoint. The identity and cocycle laws are exactly the coherence laws used in constructing and propagating the component maps.

statement_change.what: The inverse-image comparison reverses p and q. For an order map α:[p]→[q], the diagram indexed by Δ^op has f_α:Sh(E_q)→Sh(E_p), so f_α^{-1} takes a_p^{-1}G, not a_q^{-1}G. The old displayed composite is ill-typed for unequal fibres; it also cannot propagate a degree-zero map to degree one. Stacks Tag 0D70 explicitly writes f_φ^{-1} a_m^{-1}G = a_n^{-1}G for φ:[m]→[n].
